title: Effective affine fpqc descent of schemes with a compatible ample module
statement: Let $B\to C$ be a faithfully flat homomorphism of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ring-map], and set $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $S'=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X'\to S'$ be a quasi-compact scheme morphism (inverse images of affine opens are quasi-compact) [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with descent datum $\alpha$ relative to $S'/S$ [def-pd-descent-datum]. Let $M'$ be an ample invertible $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Suppose $\alpha$ is equipped with an isomorphism from $p_0^*M'$ to the pullback of $p_1^*M'$ along $\alpha$, on $p_0^*X'$, whose two composites agree over $S'\times_SS'\times_SS'$ [def-pc-module-pullback, def-pc-fibre-product]. Then there are an $S$-scheme $X$, an invertible module $M$ on $X$, and an isomorphism $(X,M)\times_SS'\simeq(X',M')$ inducing both prescribed data [def-pc-base-change]. The module $M$ is ample. No Noetherian, finite-presentation or properness assumption is made.

source.place: BLR 6.1 Theorem 7 and its graded-section-algebra proof, printed p.138 (PDF p.144), affine-base specialization. Compatible invertible modules, rather than projectivity without a polarization, are the input. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: Put $p:S'\to S$. Faithful flatness implies flatness of $B\to C$ by its definition. The affine flatness criterion and surjectivity of the spectrum map show that $p$ is flat and surjective. It is affine, hence quasi-compact; thus its singleton is fpqc. More explicitly, over any affine open $V\subset S$, its inverse image is affine and surjects onto $V$, so this one affine open witnesses the fpqc covering condition. Ampleness makes $X'$ separated by [lem-weil-pbc-ample-scheme-separated]. Together with quasi-compactness of $X'\to S'$ and affineness of $S'$, this gives the quasi-compact, quasi-separated hypotheses needed for flat base change. The projections from the double and triple products of $S'$ over $S$ are fpqc, and in particular flat, by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms].

For each $n\geq0$ put $E'_n=f'_*((M')^{\otimes n})$, where $f':X'\to S'$. These are quasi-coherent by [lem-pc-finite-support-hi], since tensor powers of an invertible module are locally free of rank one. Apply [lem-pc-flat-base-change-cohom] in degree zero to each projection $S'\times_SS'\to S'$. It identifies $p_i^*E'_n$ with the direct image of the corresponding tensor pullback of $(M')^{\otimes n}$. The specified scheme isomorphism $\alpha$ and the $n$th tensor power of its module isomorphism therefore induce $p_0^*E'_n\simeq p_1^*E'_n$. On the triple product both composites send a pulled-back section to the section obtained by the corresponding composite of the prescribed module isomorphisms. Their equality is exactly the assumed module cocycle; the base-change maps here are the canonical maps, so are obtained by pulling back sections. Thus these are descent data on $E'_n$. By [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] obtain quasi-coherent $E_n$ on $S$ and compatible isomorphisms $p^*E_n\simeq E'_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], putting $A_n=\Gamma(S,E_n)$ gives $C\otimes_B A_n\simeq\Gamma(X',(M')^{\otimes n})$, sending $c\otimes a$ to $c\widetilde a$. The section $\widetilde a$ is invariant under the prescribed pair datum, as an equality of sections on the double pullback.

We check the geometry of nonvanishing opens before using the invariant sections. Put $G=\Gamma_*(X',M')$. By [lem-sc-ample-finite-affine-cover] choose a finite cover by affine $X'_{s_j}$ for positive-degree homogeneous $s_j$. The morphism $r:X'\to\operatorname{Proj}(G)$ of [lem-sc-ample-proj-local-chart] has $r^{-1}D_+(s_j)=X'_{s_j}$ and is an isomorphism on each such chart. These isomorphisms glue with the restrictions of $r$ to an isomorphism onto the open union $\bigcup_jD_+(s_j)$: on an overlap both inverses are inverses to that same restricted morphism. Hence $r$ is an open immersion. The map is over $S'$: the constants $C\to G_0$ act by the structural sections on $X'$, and the chart localization maps send each constant to that structural section.

source.place: Tags 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), 01Q1 (lemma-ample-immersion-into-proj), proof by the finite affine section charts

proof.text: For any $n>0$ and $s\in\Gamma(X',(M')^{\otimes n})$, the preceding map embeds $X'_s$ as an open in the affine $C$-scheme $D_+(s)=\operatorname{Spec}(G_{(s)})$. The opens $X'_{s_j}\cap X'_s$ are affine by [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] and form a finite cover of $X'_s$, so $X'_s$ is quasi-compact. This is a quasi-compact open immersion into an affine $S'$-scheme. Apply the reverse implication of [lem-trf-quasi-affine-relative-spec-embedding] (the affine $C$-algebra $G_{(s)}$ supplies the quasi-coherent algebra on $S'$) to see that $X'_s\to S'$ is quasi-affine. In particular this holds for every invariant $\widetilde a$ from Step 2. No claim that an arbitrary $X'_s$ is affine is needed.

source.place: Tags 01PZ and 01Q1; Tag 01PV (lemma-affine-cap-s-open); morphisms.tex characterization of quasi-affine morphisms by an open immersion into an affine morphism (Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine)

proof.text: For every $x\in X'$, ampleness gives $n>0$ and a section $s$ of $(M')^{\otimes n}$ nonvanishing at $x$. Step 2 expresses $s=\sum_{j=1}^t c_j\widetilde a_j$ with $c_j\in C$ and $a_j\in A_n$. If all $\widetilde a_j$ vanished in the one-dimensional residue-field fibre of $(M')^{\otimes n}$ at $x$, this sum would vanish there too. Thus $x\in X'_{\widetilde a_j}$ for some $j$. The opens $U_{n,a}=X'_{\widetilde a}$, for all $n>0$ and $a\in A_n$, consequently cover $X'$. Invariance of $\widetilde a$ makes these opens stable under $\alpha$: pullback preserves whether a section generates a rank-one module, and a module isomorphism preserves generation. Restricting $\alpha$ therefore gives an isomorphism between the two pullbacks of $U_{n,a}$; its cocycle is the restriction of the given cocycle. For every test scheme the inclusion $U_{n,a}\to X'$ intertwines transport, because that restricted isomorphism is obtained by factoring the original isomorphism through the same open subschemes.

source.place: BLR 6.1 Theorem 7, printed p.138, finite linear combination and invariant nonvanishing-open argument; local PDF WANTED, primary scan read online at the URL of the item source.

proof.text: Step 4 makes every $U_{n,a}\to S'$ quasi-affine, and Step 5 supplies its restricted descent datum. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-fpqc-effective-descent] to $p:S'\to S$ and each such datum. Its hypotheses require only a singleton fpqc cover and a quasi-affine morphism, not finite presentation. Apply [lem-pd-effective-invariant-open-cover] to these effective restricted data and their transport-compatible inclusions from Step 5. It gives an $S$-scheme $X$ and an isomorphism $X\times_SS'\simeq X'$ inducing exactly $\alpha$. This gluing step includes all overlaps; no affine-intersection assumption on the cover of $X'$ has been introduced.

Under the chosen effective identification, the map $q:X'\to X$ is the base change of $p$. It is an fpqc covering by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering-axioms]. The fibre product $X'\times_X X'$ identifies with $X'\times_SS'$, using $\alpha$ to identify the second $X'$ projection. Consequently the prescribed module isomorphism is an ordinary descent datum for $M'$ along $q$, and its cocycle is exactly the one in the hypothesis. Clause (3) of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] supplies an invertible $M$ on $X$ and $q^*M\simeq M'$ compatible with that specified datum. Combined with Step 6, this gives the required pair isomorphism inducing both prescribed data.

source.place: Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent) and descent of locally free modules of rank one; topologies.tex fpqc base-change axiom

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-space-relative-ampleness-fpqc-descent] to the scheme $X\to S$, regarded as an algebraic space, with its ordinary invertible module $M$, and the singleton fpqc covering $S'\to S$. The cited statement explicitly includes the ordinary-scheme interpretation of line modules and requires neither properness nor Noetherianity. On the cover its pullback is $M'$, ample on $X'$. Since $X'\to S'$ is quasi-compact with $S'$ affine, [lem-trf-affine-base-ample-canonical-data] shows that $M'$ restricted to the inverse image of every affine open $W\subseteq S'$ is ample, i.e. $M'$ is relatively ample over $S'$ in the sense of the cited descent statement. Thus $M$ is relatively ample over $S$. Since $S=\operatorname{Spec}B$ is affine, the definition of relative ampleness in that cited statement says that $M$ is ample on $X$. Empty schemes, including the zero-ring base case, are covered by the same construction: the section-cover argument is vacuous and the effective gluing is empty.
